_meta.purpose: 3D-verified ground truth for item D (the Echancree tablet), transcribed from the INSCRIBE project's re-reading. Used to check the Barthel/C.E.I.P.P. reading of the same object sign by sign: this is the only tablet in the corpus for which a sub-millimetre 3D model has produced a published, independent transcription.
_meta.citation: Lastilla, L., Ravanelli, R., Valerio, M. & Ferrara, S. (2022). Modelling the Rongorongo tablets: a new transcription of the Echancree tablet and the foundation for decipherment attempts. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities 37(2): 497-518. doi:10.1093/llc/fqab070
_meta.license: CC BY-NC (Oxford University Press on behalf of EADH). What is stored here is the transcription -- a catalogue of readings, cited -- not the article's drawings, figures or 3D models, none of which are reproduced.
_meta.transcribed_from: Sections 4.1.1 (side A) and 4.1.2 (side B), pp. 509-510, verified against both the publisher HTML and the open-access PDF at cris.unibo.it.

notation.] [: line begins / ends at a broken or lost edge
notation.. :: Barthel's linking and stacking, as in his own system
notation./: two equally possible transcriptions of one element, e.g. 381/741 (Barthel's 381 and 741 are probably variants of one sign)
notation.*: the paper's bullet: uncertainty about one glyph, or about one digit-position (body part) of a 200-700 series glyph. '68*' = one of the five signs in the 680 series, lower portion not preserved.
notation.( ): an element's internal composition or an editorial equation, e.g. 173(=5.225/325)
notation.[...]: an indeterminate stretch of lost signs

_meta.codes_are: Barthel's ORIGINAL system, unpadded (1, 60, 700), NOT the C.E.I.P.P. extended system. Zero-fill before comparing with tablets_ceipp.json.
_meta.KNOWN_LOSS: The paper marks doubtful readings by UNDERLINING. Underlining survives neither the HTML nor the PDF text extraction, so it is absent here. Any element in this file may be a doubtful reading in the original; consult the article before treating a single element as settled.
uncertain_transcriptions: Db3, between '4.94a/116' and the following '2': the source renders this as '- -' (PDF) / '--' (HTML). It is most likely a bullet element whose glyph was dropped by both text extractions, but it has not been confirmed against the printed page. Recorded verbatim below; do not count on it. compare_echancree.py treats it as one INDETERMINATE element rather than as nothing, which correctly excludes Db3 from its position-by-position pass -- resolve this against the printed page to bring the line back into the comparison.
